name: Seagirt IFC reference alignment
why: The IFC's IfcMapConversion places the model as if the image it was drawn on were north-up, so the quay comes out east-west and offshore. That image is rotated about 38 degrees. This alignment replaces the file's georeferencing with a fit to the real terminal; it is a calibration, not authoritative georeferencing.
method: Similarity transform (rotation, uniform scale, translation), computed in a local WGS84 east/north frame. IFC model metres map to pixels of the reference image the model was drawn from; two quay corners in that image are tied to their OpenStreetMap coordinates.

ifcFromReferenceImage.relation: x = (px - 974) * 5/3, y = -(py - 456) * 5/3 (metres; origin = main substation point)
ifcFromReferenceImage.evidence: Fitted to 29 equipment positions in the image (the what-if artifact's node table): residuals 0.6 m in x and up to 4.4 m in y, except elements whose geometry is offset from their symbol (main transformers, crane structures).

referenceImage: terminal.jpg (1417 x 876 px) from the 'Seagirt Terminal Power What-If' artifact: Cesium ion view, Google imagery

controlPoints.name: West quay corner (angled west edge meets the berth face)
controlPoints.source: OpenStreetMap way/87334858 (Seagirt Marine Terminal outline), vertex

controlPoints.name: Southeast quay corner at Colgate Creek
controlPoints.source: OpenStreetMap way/87334858 (Seagirt Marine Terminal outline), vertex

check: The whole OpenStreetMap terminal outline and road network, drawn onto the reference image through this transform, follow the quay, the Colgate Creek edge, the north boundary and the container-yard lanes.
accuracy: About 5 to 10 m: OpenStreetMap outline accuracy and picking the corners to about 2 px. Scale 0.96545 because the model was built from the image's scale bar (60 px per 100 m); the terminal measures 62.1 px per 100 m in that image.
doesNotChange: The electrical twin's assets, graph and positions; the IFC file; the converted geometry.
